sources.title: Official biography: birth, MGIMO education, SOCAR, parliament, premiership, party leadership and presidential elections
sources.findings: Read the official biography’s birth, education and career chronology. It gives 24 December 1961 in Baku, MGIMO study in 1977–1982, postgraduate work, history thesis in 1985 and teaching until 1990; these are biographical statements, not inspected university records. SOCAR vice-president and first vice-president roles cover 1994–August 2003, without a separate first-vice-president promotion date. Do not call him SOCAR president. Parliament elections in 1995 and 2000, premiership on 4 August 2003 and party chairmanship in 2005 are separated. The five presidential election dates support fifth-term chronology; official vote percentages are not independent electoral-quality findings and are omitted.

sources.title: 31 October 2003: Aliyev sworn in as president, succeeding his father after a contested election
sources.findings: Read the short contemporaneous RFE/RL inauguration report dated 31 October 2003. It explicitly says he was inaugurated that day, succeeded his father Heydar/Heidar Aliyev, and followed the widely criticized 15 October election. The election date, inauguration date and short preceding premiership are distinct. The article attributes the vote tally to election officials; the dossier does not independently endorse that percentage or infer a court judgment invalidating the election.

sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Global Legal Monitor
sources.title: Indexed March 2017 legal account: first vice-president appointment and September 2016 constitutional amendments
sources.findings: Read indexed Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor excerpts of the 24 March 2017 article. They explicitly identify the 21 February appointment of his wife, new constitutional article 103(1), September 2016 creation of vice-presidential offices and extension of the presidential term from five to seven years. The body returned 403, so no full-article or underlying constitutional-text audit is claimed. Presidential term length and removal of limits on the number of terms are different changes; no claim that term limits were abolished in 2016 is made. March publication is not the appointment date.

sources.title: 21 February 2017 Security Council meeting: appointment of Mehriban Aliyeva as First Vice-President
sources.findings: Read the 21 February 2017 official Security Council meeting account, especially the announcement and introductory biographical passages. It records the president’s appointment of Mehriban Aliyeva that day and her previous parliamentary and Heydar Aliyev Foundation roles. His praise of her competence and claimed programme successes is political speech, not an independent appraisal. This is a historical appointment, not an assumption about every later office or an attribution of his wife’s achievements to him.

sources.publisher: Presidents of Azerbaijan and Russia and Prime Minister of Armenia
sources.title: 10 November 2020 trilateral ceasefire statement and arrangements
sources.findings: Read the nine operative provisions of the 10 November 2020 tripartite statement published by the Azerbaijani presidency. They specify a ceasefire from 00:00 Moscow time that day, territorial-transfer arrangements, Russian peacekeepers, displaced persons, exchanges and transport links. The original text’s planned dates and renewable peacekeeper term are historical provisions, not proof of their later fulfillment or continuing deployment in November 2026. No assertion that the statement permanently resolved all disputes, completed all returns or constituted the later peace treaty is made.

sources.title: Indexed refugee response overview: over 100000 arrivals from Karabakh in one week in September 2023
sources.findings: Read the indexed UNHCR Armenia response overview, which explicitly places over 100000 arrivals within one week in September 2023. The UNHCR Japan 6 October 2023 indexed release connects the exodus to Azerbaijani military operations. Opening both pages and the emergency-requirements PDF returned 429, so their full bodies were not reviewed. The 19 September operation date is corroborated in the ICJ summary. Do not substitute later total refugee stocks for this one-week flow or infer that every displaced person’s property claim has been adjudicated.

sources.title: Summary of the 17 November 2023 provisional-measures order in Armenia v. Azerbaijan
sources.findings: Read selected background, rights/plausibility, provisional-measures and operative-clause passages of the Court’s summary of the 17 November 2023 order. The document distinguishes Armenia’s requested measures and allegations from the Court’s actual orders. Operative paragraphs cover safe return and departure, protection from force or intimidation, preservation and consideration of identity/property records, and an eight-week reporting obligation. These are provisional measures under CERD, not a final merits ruling, a genocide finding or a criminal conviction of Aliyev. Do not replace the actual reporting period with the applicant’s requested one-month/quarterly schedule. The full underlying order, later case developments and every dissent were not reviewed.

sources.publisher: OSCE ODIHR and OSCE Parliamentary Assembly
sources.title: 8 February 2024 presidential-election observation findings: restrictive environment, absent pluralism and procedural shortcomings
sources.findings: Read the 8 February 2024 ODIHR/OSCE PA statement concerning the previous day’s early presidential election. It credits efficient preparations while identifying absent genuine pluralism, restrictions on critical voices, noncompetitive alternatives and serious polling/counting safeguards problems. These are attributed observer findings, not a judicial annulment or a statement about the separate September 2024 parliamentary election. The presence of six other candidates does not establish effective competition. No full final observation report or precinct-level dataset was audited.

sources.title: 14 February 2024 inauguration ceremony at the Milli Majlis
sources.findings: Read the date, opening inauguration account, Constitutional Court confirmation passage and oath sequence of the official 14 February 2024 report. It records the completed ceremony at the Milli Majlis, following the 7 February election and 13 February confirmation. It is not an advance invitation. The president’s subsequent claims about achievements and support are his speech, not adopted as independent facts; the whole lengthy speech and videos were not reviewed.

sources.title: World Report 2026, Azerbaijan: events of 2025, independent media and civil society
sources.findings: Read World Report 2026’s Azerbaijan introduction and freedom-of-expression/media passages. The chapter explicitly reviews events of 2025 and criticizes repression of media, opposition and civil society. The dossier attributes these assessments to HRW and does not relabel them as a complete November 2026 conditions audit or individual judicial verdicts. Specific journalists’ later case outcomes were not checked and are not presented as current custody facts. Its broad description of the Washington process is distinguished from the primary statement’s more precise declaration-versus-initialed-draft terminology.

sources.publisher: United States, Armenia and Azerbaijan; Armenian foreign ministry publication
sources.title: 10 August 2026 anniversary statement distinguishing the signed 2025 declaration from the initialed draft peace agreement
sources.findings: Read the 10 August 2026 US-Armenia-Azerbaijan anniversary statement published by the Armenian foreign ministry, including its explicit account of the 2025 White House summit. Aliyev and Pashinyan signed the joint declaration; the foreign ministers initialed the draft peace and interstate-relations agreement. August 8 is independently specified in both November meeting accounts. Political claims about ending conflict and infrastructure progress do not establish treaty ratification, completed construction or independently audited trade totals. A Nobel nomination is not an award; the nomination and financial/trade figures are not imported into the biography.

sources.title: 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting with Aliyev: peace agenda, borders, transport and trade
sources.findings: Read the Armenian prime minister’s 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting release. It records an actual meeting with Aliyev at the ninth European Political Community summit and discussion of peace, transport, trade and border delimitation. The forthcoming electricity-grid interconnection is a prospective matter. Cargo totals are official claims rather than independent audit results and are omitted. This supplies recent activity evidence; it does not announce ratification or entry into force of the full peace agreement.

sources.title: 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting with Pashinyan: connectivity planning and continuing dialogue
sources.findings: Read the Azerbaijani presidency’s corresponding 12 November 2026 Dublin meeting account. It corroborates the participants and event, and describes TRIPP railway/highway planning and design, prospects for connectivity, future grid links and transboundary-water cooperation. These are not proof that every construction project is complete, that Armenian sovereignty was transferred, or that all disputed legal questions are settled. The two government accounts agree on the meeting but remain official reports; no image pixels, recording or independent cargo dataset was inspected.

The image is dated December 2025; 1 January 2026 is the upload/crop date, not a verified capture day. Toghrul R is uploader/cropper, not the credited photographer. Parent is 2500×1706 (3.44 MB); crop is 1022×1323 (1.18 MB), described as a 59-percent horizontal and 22-percent vertical reduction. The old cache record lists 156089 bytes and is absent, not proof of possession of the original. Original download on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000. Identity, original colour, crop and actual resolution/sharpness remain visually unreviewed. Preserve source credit, licence link and a modification notice.
